title: The C Major Scale
description: Play your first scale using only the white keys, then stack three of its notes into a chord.

steps.title: All white keys
steps.description: The C major scale is C, D, E, F, G, A, B, and then C again. No black keys at all, which makes it the easiest scale to see and play. Every other major scale uses this same pattern of steps, just starting on a different note.

steps.title: Find middle C
steps.description: Start on middle C. Find the group of two black keys near the middle of the keyboard and press the white key just to their left.
steps.hint: It's the white key touching the left side of the two black keys.

steps.title: Add the E
steps.description: Keep C and add E, two white keys up. Press them together. That gap is called a major third, and it already sounds bright.
steps.hint: Skip over D. Thumb on C and middle finger on E feels natural.

steps.title: Now the whole scale
steps.description: Walk up the white keys from C to the next C: C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C. That's eight keys, one at a time. Take it slowly and keep it even.
steps.hint: Try thumb, index, middle on C, D, E, then tuck your thumb under to land on F and carry on up to the pinky.

steps.title: Stack C, E and G
steps.description: Play C, E and G together. That's a C major chord: every other note of the scale, stacked up.
steps.hint: Thumb on C, middle finger on E, pinky on G. Any octave works.

steps.title: Count them up
steps.description: How many different notes are in a major scale? (The C at the top doesn't count twice.)
